_comment: Log-based alert. Does NOT require Managed Prometheus - it reads Kubernetes events, which are exported to Cloud Logging for free. Create the log-based metric first (see monitoring/README.md).

documentation.content:
A DEPLOYMENT IS NOT PROGRESSING.

This fires on Kubernetes events indicating pods cannot start: FailedScheduling, ImagePullBackOff, CrashLoopBackOff, FailedCreate.

First command:
  kubectl get events -n orders --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -20

Then match the reason:
  FailedScheduling    -> no node has capacity, or taint/affinity mismatch  (TROUBLESHOOTING 1)
  ImagePullBackOff    -> tag missing, IAM, wrong registry path             (TROUBLESHOOTING 2)
  CrashLoopBackOff    -> app exits at boot; kubectl logs POD --previous    (TROUBLESHOOTING 3)
  FailedCreate        -> quota, or a missing ConfigMap/Secret              (TROUBLESHOOTING 8)

If this fired during a pipeline deploy, --atomic should have rolled back
automatically. Confirm rather than assume:
  helm history orders-api -n orders

If --atomic did NOT roll back, the release is stuck. Roll back manually:
  ./scripts/rollback.sh -n orders
